note:
Browsing 'Bounds on the Satisfiability Threshold for Power Law Distributed Random SAT' by Friedrich, Krohmer, Rothernberger, Sauerwald, Sutton:
* $m$ clauses, $n$ variables, ratio $m/n$
* $\beta \sim (2k-1)/(k-1)$, power law exponent
* $\beta \le (2k-1)/(k-1) - \epsilon$ has $k$ largest variables in too many clauses ($2^k$ finite, causes contradiction, $O(\log n)$ clauses of top $k$ variables)
* for some fixed ratio $\kappa = m/n$, $\beta \ge (2k-1)/(k-1) + \epsilon$ has large variance of variables in clauses which can be reduced down to a 2-sat instance
So the idea is that if $\beta$ is too small, this generates a lot of grumblers which cause contradictions. For $\beta$ too high, this causes a lot of gabbers, which allows for easy influence and is easily satisfied. When grumblers and gabbers are kept in check while maintaining clause-variable ratio below a critical value, then instances aren't almost sure sat or unsat (by this method). Not sure what the region looks like or what the values of $\kappa$ are.
